history.summary: FLAG - NOT A HINDU TEMPLE: no web source documents any temple named "Dombe Temple". Dombe Wari is a natural lake/sacred folklore site on the Emangre-to-Wari Chora route in South Garo Hills, Meghalaya, visited just before the Wari Chora parking spot on the Emangre/Paromgre off-road route. In Garo folklore it is the site of the legend of Dombe Rani - a beautiful woman who lived in a treehouse with her husband Joreng and was claimed by mermen, after which the calm Dombe Wari (a deep river pool) was formed; a Doordarshan Tura film on the legend exists. It is a cultural/natural attraction of the Garo Hills, not a place of Hindu worship - keep-or-drop decision needed for a Hindu-temples dataset. CSV town "Baghmara" is the district headquarters gateway, not the site's location: Dombe Wari is in the Wari Chora/Emangre area, far from Baghmara town.

name: Dombe Wari (CSV row name: Dombe Temple)
town_description: Baghmara is the district headquarters of South Garo Hills, Meghalaya, and the base for Wari Chora visits. Dombe Wari lies on the off-road Emangre-to-Wari Chora route, deep in the South Garo Hills jungle.
tradition: Not a Hindu temple - a Garo folklore/natural lake site; keep-or-drop decision needed.

travel.airport: Guwahati Airport is the usual gateway (~250 km to the region); Shillong Airport is an alternative.
travel.railway: No railway station nearby; nearest major station is Guwahati, Assam.
travel.road: Tura to Baghmara to Emangre, then off-road 4x4 from Emangre/Paromgre toward Wari Chora; Dombe Wari is on the right just before the Wari Chora parking spot. A local guide and agent are advised.

visitor_information.best_time: October to April (dry season); monsoon makes off-road routes dangerous.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Natural site - daylight visits; hire a local guide (verify locally). Note: coordinates are district-level approximate (Emangre-Wari Chora route) - verify on ground. Media: no reliable site-specific image found after genuine searching.
